new_statements.quote: Stress is phonemic in HJ, e.g., such contrasts as: únā "him (direct object)," unāˊ "they." [Number:] HJ nouns have one type of plural ending for both animates and inanimates: -āˊ, e.g., šāx-ā "horns," yehudi-ā "Jews." There are two indefinite markers: the number ye(y) "one" (yey šarbat "a syrup") and an unstressed -ì (miāˊn-e bāˊγi "in a garden") [...] [Negation:] Negation is expressed by a stressed, prefixed né-~ná- that comes just before the verb root: néšzunā "he/she couldn't," nédārān "I don't have" vānábo "it didn't become."

new_statements.rule_in_words: The source states only that stress is phonemic (contrastive) in the Hamadan Jewish dialect, illustrated by únā 'him (obj.)' vs. unāˊ 'they' — a contrast created by the stressed plural suffix -āˊ, so the contrast is morphological rather than lexical. No positional rule is given, but every stress-marked example is Persian-type: nouns stressed on the stem-final syllable (gardán-e, ésm-eš, píl-ā, vecé-š-ā, bāˊγi with unstressed indefinite -i), plural -āˊ stressed, verbal prefixes bé-/né- and preverbs (vāˊ-) stressed, durative e- unstressed. A reviewer may prefer to file this as fixed-final with morphologically conditioned exceptions; Gindin's second-hand survey line ('ultimate in Persian and other Jewish Iranian dialects') points the same way.
new_statements.exceptions: Unstressed indefinite -ì; stressed negative prefix né-~ná-; stressed subjunctive/imperative bé- and preverbs in the examples; unstressed durative marker e- (marked as unstressed in the verb tables). No general exception list.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in a descriptive sketch of the dialect of the Jews of Hamadān (HJ) with notes on Tuyserkān (TJ); based on Abrahamian 1936, Yarshater's field notes and Stilo's own 2001-02 fieldwork with the last speakers. The Borujerd Jewish dialect (Yarshater 1989), grouped under jude1268 by Glottolog, is not described in this article.
new_statements.identity_note: Stilo 2003 describes the Jewish dialect of Hamadān (HJ) and, in an appendix, that of Tuyserkān (TJ), both under Glottolog jude1268 (Judeo-Hamadani-Borujerdi); the Borujerd Jewish dialect that Glottolog folds into the same languoid is described only by Yarshater 1989 and Borjian 2025, neither of which could be opened. The statement therefore rests on the Hamadan variety.

sources.note: Phonology section: "Stress is phonemic in HJ, e.g., such contrasts as: únā 'him (direct object),' unāˊ 'they.'" Elsewhere: plural suffix -āˊ is stressed; indefinite -ì is unstressed (miāˊn-e bāˊγi); negative prefix né-~ná- is stressed; marked examples show stem-final stress on nouns (gardán-e, ésm-eš, píl-ā, vecé-š-ā) and stressed bé-/preverb (bé-dān-ferāte, vāˊ-š-parsā). No general positional rule stated. Direct fetch of iranicaonline.org returns HTTP 403 (Cloudflare); text obtained through the r.jina.ai page-to-markdown proxy, which dropped a few spaces (file reads "Stressis").

Tertiary. "The suprasegmentals of the language, including rhythm, tone, intonation, and stress, are influenced by the Persian Hamadani dialect" — cited to Gholami 2022 (Iranian Studies 54:769–805). Used for its bibliography (Stilo 2003, Borjian 2014, Borjian 2025, Gholami 2022).
